source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMTERTIUM, De aeternitate Dei. Sequitur sextum DEI attributum, aeternitas videlicet, quae est summa illius perfectio, qua expers est finitae durationis. Aeternitatis vox notat proprie durationem stativam sine principio, medio, fine, sine fluxu praeteriti, praesentis, futuri. Ex antiquis Boethius ita definit: Aeternitas est interminabilis vitae tota simul et perfecta possessio, vel est duratio interminabilis, indivisibilis et independens.
english: CHAPTER THIRTEEN. On the eternity of God.

There follows GOD's sixth attribute, namely eternity, which is His highest perfection, by which He is free from finite duration. The word eternity properly notes a standing duration without beginning, middle, end, without flux of past, present, future.
Among the ancients Boethius defines thus: Eternity is the whole, simultaneous, and perfect possession of interminable life — or it is interminable, indivisible, and independent duration.

source_text: Differt a tempore, ut auctor est Clemens Alexandrinus. Improprie tribuitur tum rebus quae etsi principium temporis habeant nullum tamen finem habebunt, ut Angeli, daemones, animae rationales; tum iis quae diuturnae sunt. Hinc Albertus Magnus: Dicitur aeternum duobus modis, per essentiam scilicet et per participationem. Per essentiam solus Deus aeternus est. Per participationem autem dicitur aeternum esse id quod aeternitatis aliquam proprietatem participat — incommutabilitatem et carentiam finis — analogice, non univoce.
english: It differs from time, as Clement of Alexandria is authority. Improperly it is attributed both to things which, though they have a beginning of time, will yet have no end — as angels, demons, rational souls — and to those which are long-lasting.

Hence Albert the Great: Eternal is said in two ways, namely by essence and by participation. By essence God alone is eternal. But by participation that is said to be eternal which participates some property of eternity — immutability and lack of end — analogically, not univocally.

source_text: Demonstro autem Deum proprie aeternum esse, id est, ab anteriore et posteriore interminabilem, nunquam coepisse, nunquam desiturum esse. PRIMO, a sacrae Scripturae testimonio, Psal. XC.2; Isa. LVII.16; Gen. XXI.33; Dan. VII.13; Rom. XVI.26; I Tim. I.17. SECUNDO, ab essentiae immutabilitate. TERTIO, ab absoluta existendi necessitate. QUARTO, ab independentia. QUINTO, a naturae simplicitate. SEXTO, a consensu catholico — Athenagoras, Cyprianus, Augustinus, Gregorius, Anselmus, Bernhardus, Albertus Magnus. SEPTIMO, a calculo philosophorum — Aristoteles Metaph. XII.7.
english: I demonstrate that God is properly eternal — that is, interminable from before and after, never having begun, never about to cease. FIRST, from the testimony of sacred Scripture: Psalm 90:2; Isaiah 57:16; Genesis 21:33; Daniel 7:13; Romans 16:26; 1 Timothy 1:17. SECOND, from the immutability of essence. THIRD, from the absolute necessity of existing. FOURTH, from independence.

FIFTH, from simplicity of nature. SIXTH, from catholic consent — Athenagoras, Cyprian, Augustine, Gregory, Anselm, Bernard, Albert the Great. SEVENTH, from the reckoning of the philosophers — Aristotle, Metaphysics XII.7.

source_text: CONTRADICIT huic doctrinae CONR. VORSTIUS Notis ad disp. III. de Deo p.226, vulgarem sententiam de aeternitate tota simul existente falsam esse contendens. Quapropter fundamenta et regulas quasdam hic trademus. 1. Aeternitas Dei non est accidens, sed substantia Dei — est enim reipsa nihil aliud quam duratio Dei, et duratio nihil aliud quam existentia durans. 2. Aeternitas Dei est indivisibilis et tota simul, neque habet partes sibi invicem succedentes. 3. Aeternitas Dei, cum sit indivisibilis, necessario existit cum omnibus temporum differentiis — non quod omnes partes temporis simul inter se existant, sed quod singulae partes temporis dum actu sunt existunt cum aeternitate.
english: Conrad Vorstius contradicts this doctrine in Notes on Disputation III On God p. 226, contending that the common opinion of eternity existing all at once is false. For that reason we hand down certain foundations and rules here.

1. God's eternity is not an accident, but God's substance — for it is in reality nothing other than God's duration, and duration nothing other than persevering existence. 2. God's eternity is indivisible and entirely simultaneous, and has no parts succeeding one another. 3. God's eternity, being indivisible, necessarily exists with all differences of times — not that all parts of time exist together among themselves, but that each part of time, while it is in act, exists with eternity.

source_text: 4. Deus in tempore agit, non subjacendo tempori, sed rem finitam subiciendo tempori. 5. In Deo est prius et posterius, non ratione essentiae aut temporis, sed ratione ordinis inter personas S.S. Trinitatis et inter attributa ejus, ratione nostri intellectus. Opera Dei ad intra sunt actus semper durans; at opera ad extra finiuntur pro libera Dei voluntate. 6. Omnia sunt Deo praesentia, non ratione existentiae, sed notitiae. 7. Anni aeterni et dies aeternitatis de Deo non dicuntur propter divisionem aeternitatis in se, sed propter divisionem perpetuitatis et temporis, quae continet sub se excellenter. 8. Aeternitatem Dei debemus imitari constanti activitate boni, indefinenti appetitione beatae aeternitatis. Hac propter caput de aeternitate Dei hac monela obsigno: AETERNITATEM COGITA.
english: 4. God acts in time not by being subject to time, but by subjecting a finite thing to time. 5. In God there is prior and posterior not by reason of essence or time, but by reason of order among the persons of the Holy Trinity and among His attributes, by reason of our intellect. God's inward works are an act always lasting; but outward works are finished according to God's free will.

6. All things are present to God not by reason of existence, but of knowledge. 7. Eternal years and days of eternity are not said of God because of a division of eternity in itself, but because of the division of perpetuity and time, which He contains under Himself excellently. 8. We ought to imitate God's eternity by constant activity of the good, by unceasing desire of blessed eternity. For that reason I seal the chapter on God's eternity with this monition: THINK ON ETERNITY.
